item.title: Southern Ocean may flip from carbon sink to carbon source under mitigation scenarios
item.description: Plans to limit the global temperature rise to 1.5°C above preindustrial levels depend on reaching net-zero emissions and, in many cases, actively removing carbon dioxide (CO2) from the air. While this helps limit extreme weather, sea level rise, ecosystem loss and the risk of triggering irreversible climate tipping points, a new study, published in Science Advances, finds that reducing CO2 levels may have an unexpected effect. Climate simulations used in the study suggest that the Southern Ocean around Antarctica may switch from being an important carbon sink to being a prolific source of… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: En 1987, Costa Rica había perdido la mitad de su bosque. Hoy es el ejemplo mundial en revertir la deforestación
item.description: En 1940, Costa Rica era un auténtico vergel: el 75% del país estaba cubierto de bosque tropical . En 1987, esa cobertura forestal se había desplomado hasta apenas un 21%. Casi medio siglo de devastadora deforestación que puede ser la sentencia de muerte para biodiversidad. En la era del cambio climático, poca broma con la desertificación . Sin embargo, el país centroamericano decidió ponerse manos a la obra y en poco más de 30 años consiguió dar marcha atrás con éxito : hoy más de la mitad de su territorio vuelve a ser bosque. Adiós a la selva en medio siglo . ¿Qué pasó desde los años 40… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Kenya: Crocodiles pushed towards homes by rising lakes
item.description: Climate change is forcing Kenya's wildlife officers to go on a crocodile hunt on the shores of Lake Baringo in a bid to curb growing human-wildlife conflict. Lakes in Kenya's Rift Valley have risen to levels not seen in at least half a century, pushing the reptiles towards human homes. Officers are tasked with trapping the animals and relocating them — an operation as tricky as it is dangerous. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: As trust in institutions wavers, experts say local, collective action is more effective in driving change Wildfires, excess deaths, hosepipe bans, school closures: this summer many British people have experienced the often devastating effects of the climate crisis in ways they had not before. item.title: Artist delights in beautiful ‘mess’ and dead trees of England’s rewilding sites
item.description: Rebecca Howard spent two years visiting projects and painting landscapes that feature in West Sussex exhibition Rewilding areas do not usually conform to traditional notions of beauty in England’s green and pleasant land. Detractors may bewail the beaver-felled trees, untidy scrub, deadwood, weeds, mud and “mess”. But a new exhibition highlights the aesthetic delights that can be discovered on rewilding sites where fungi grows on dying trees, water buffalo gather in new wetlands and brown-watered beaver pools flood once-desiccated fields. item.title: 10,000 years of wheat and barley selection reveal shared climate-adaptation genes
item.description: Research teams from INRAE, the University of Clermont Auvergne and the CNRS have reconstructed 10 ancient genomes (paleogenomes) that are the common ancestors of 84 botanical species of agronomic interest. Their work makes it possible to identify particular genes, shared across different species of plants and retained throughout their evolutionary history, that might play a key role in adapting to environmental constraints such as drought. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New study offers a detailed look at how wildfire smoke impacts Reno's air quality
item.description: With Western wildfires increasing in size, duration and intensity, millions of Americans are now exposed to wildfire smoke each year. In California, 2020 and 2021 were particularly challenging, with a 10-fold increase in fires compared with any time in the state's history. Northern Nevada is positioned to receive much of the smoke from California wildfires, and Reno residents experienced months of smoke-shrouded skies during this time. Now, a new study gives us a deeper look into the potentially hazardous chemicals lurking in this smoke. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: To monitor the amount and type of nuclear material at power plants and weapons facilities, scientists look for a special signal—the unique pattern of gamma rays emitted by specific radioactive elements. However, some of these elements also emit X-rays in the same energy range as the gamma-ray emissions, masking the signal and making nuclear stockpiles harder to assess. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Laura Iturbide, la empresaria mexicana que sobrevivió al 11-S: "Cuando salí a la calle, era como haber llegado al infierno y verlo con mis propios ojos"
item.description: Estaba alojada en el hotel que conectaba ambas torres y consiguió salir ignorando los avisos de megafonía. "Nunca he sentido algo igual en la vida y he vivido un terremoto de altísimo nivel", detalla Leer Fuente: El Mundo - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: Pablo R. Roces

item.title: Himalayan glacial lakes are growing—and so is the downstream flood risk
item.description: Dozens of glacial lakes have formed across northern India in the last three decades, while existing lakes have expanded rapidly, highlighting the need to monitor a landscape reshaped by climate change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Court rules residents of a US city don’t have a constitutional right to lead-free water
item.description: A U.S. federal court recently ruled that residents of Jackson, Mississippi, don’t have a constitutional right to truthful information from public officials, nor the right to municipal drinking water that is free of lead, a neurotoxin. “The Constitution does not provide redress for every governmental wrongdoing,” Judge Kurt D. Engelhardt of the U.S. Court of […] Fuente: Mongabay.
item.dc:creator: Shreya Dasgupta

item.title: Water isotopes reveal early drought signals in Central Amazon rainfall
item.description: The historic droughts of 2023 and 2024 in the Amazon reduced river flows and altered the region's rainfall composition. Daily monitoring in Manaus, the capital of the Brazilian state of Amazonas, revealed these changes through the use of isotopes, which act as a kind of water "fingerprint." This method demonstrated how El Niño and warming in the North Atlantic affected the origin of moisture and precipitation dynamics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Record heat and drought make this year's champagne stronger
item.description: For the first time, French champagne producers are allowed to sell their bubbly with more than 13% alcohol, as record heatwaves and drought have resulted in grapes containing unusually high levels of sugar. They fear that climate change may eventually force them to permanently rewrite the rules governing winemaking. Also in the segment, the European Central Bank raised interest rates for the second time this year amid higher energy costs, as a potential new gas crisis looms over Europe. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Francisco Moreno Carrillo: "Rol de la Cruz Roja es llegar a los lugares más alejados y difíciles"
item.description: El director ejecutivo nacional de la Cruz Roja Colombiana, Francisco Moreno Carrillo, nos contó cómo fueron sido las operaciones de la entidad para llegar con los cuerpos de rescate y llevar ayudas humanitarias a los municipios más afectados y que quedaron aislados por el terremoto de 7,4 del 10 de agosto. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Mateo Yepes Serna: "Recuerdo el polvo y el barro que tenía encima tras el terremoto en Colombia"
item.description: A un mes del terremoto en Colombia, en France 24 hablamos con Mateo Yepes Serna, un periodista manizaleño que quedó bajo los escombros de su casa en Pereira junto a su mamá. La tragedia, que le causó lesiones físicas y un fuerte trauma, también le mostró la red de apoyo que estaba a su alrededor. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Two previously unknown saucer bugs species discovered
item.description: An entomologist at the University of Missouri has discovered two saucer bug species previously unknown to science, adding to our understanding of Earth's biodiversity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Informe desde Pereira: el estado de la ciudad un mes después del terremoto
item.description: Nuestro enviado especial a Pereira, Maxime Pluvinet, nos contó cuáles han sido los cambios de la capital de Risaralda, una de las ciudades más afectadas por el terremoto de 7,4 del 10 de agosto. Edificios demolidos, escombros en las calles y edificios agrietados se ven aún en las zonas más golpeadas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Japan deploys equipment to Indonesia’s Borneo to help fight wildfires causing toxic haze
item.description: MEMPAWAH, Indonesia (AP) — A Japanese military transport ship docked on the island of Borneo on Thursday as part of a disaster relief mission to help fight wildfires in Indonesia that are causing a toxic haze impacting people’s health in other countries. Japan deployed 300 crew members, landing ship JS Kunisaki and three CH-47 helicopters, […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Focus on biodiversity conservation may offer a less divisive path to climate action in Japan
item.description: If you want to drum up support for environmental action, putting climate change front and center may not always be the best strategy. A new study by Aya Takagi and Ryosuke Nakadai of Yokohama National University suggests that support for policies that emphasize biodiversity conservation, including conservation measures that also contribute to climate goals, may be less divided along cultural lines than measures explicitly associated with climate change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Colombia: un mes después del terremoto intenta reactivar sus economías locales
item.description: El costo total de la reconstrucción de las ciudades más afectadas todavía está por calcular, pero estimaciones preliminares señalan una cifra cercana a los 10.000 millones de dólares. Los damnificados, en tanto, intentan retomar sus rutinas, pero se enfrentan a una enorme presión económica, que se suma a una crisis habitacional. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.description: The last time there were no hurricanes during the Atlantic season was before the satellite era Fuente: The Independent - World.

item.description: The fund helped Brazil reach a 10-year low in deforestation, but conservationists are bracing for a potential sharp policy U-turn. Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Un mes del terremoto en Colombia: el antes y después de la tragedia
item.description: El peor terremoto del siglo en Colombia dejó huellas imborrables en el país. Un mes después de la tragedia, en Cali y Pereira avanzan las labores de demolición de los edificios que, a pesar de no haber colapsado, quedaron gravemente dañados y completamente inhabitables. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Rewetting peatlands may curb warming-driven CO₂ emissions
item.description: Peatlands store large amounts of carbon. However, when they are drained, they can become substantial sources of the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide (CO₂). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Large protected areas help northern bird species cope with climate change
item.description: A recent study coordinated by the University of Helsinki tracked the populations of 100 bird species across Finnish protected areas. Cold-dwelling species fared better in large protected areas, while the same species saw much steeper declines in smaller ones. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Drones deliver food and remove bodies after Nepal’s flood disaster
item.description: DJI drones that already supply Mount Everest camps assist Nepal’s flood relief. Fuente: Ars Technica.

item.description: This is Part Three in a Mongabay series about trends in the offshore wind industry. Part One describes the sector’s untapped potential and gaps between installed energy generation capacity and climate goals. Part Two describes challenges the sector faces in scaling up to meet climate goals. Offshore wind farms are growing in number, with many […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: August hottest month ever recorded globally as huge El Nino emerges
item.description: Europe's climate monitor said Thursday that August was the hottest month ever recorded around the world and warned of worse to come, as an unprecedented El Nino pattern grows stronger. Global temperatures over land and sea soared to all-time highs in August and capped an extreme summer of heatwaves and wildfires that ranked the hottest on record for western Europe and the contiguous United States. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: How atmospheric events at the top of the world could have triggered two devastating California floods
item.description: In early 2017 and 2023, California experienced two catastrophic and record-breaking floods that caused billions of dollars in damage, triggered mudslides and forced thousands of people to evacuate. Why this happened left scientists scratching their heads. Both disasters struck during La Niña conditions, which normally bring drier-than-normal weather to California. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The Vashishti River, originating in the biodiversity-rich Western Ghats and flowing into the Arabian Sea along India’s western coast, has long supported traditional fishing communities. But in 2023, local fishers encountered something entirely unexpected. As they hauled a gill net into a boat, a gray body, still making faint movements, emerged tangled in the mesh, […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: As saltwater advances, Gambian farmers rethink how to protect rice fields
item.description: Every year, the villagers of Kiang Jifarong contribute labor and money to build earthen dikes using clay and mud in an effort to keep seawater out of their farms. Rice fields once stretched unbroken for 5 kilometers, about 3 miles, along the Bintang Bolong estuary here in western Gambia. For generations, families cultivated rice on […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Simple farming changes boost wheat yields in drought-prone areas
item.description: In drought-prone regions of Ethiopia, growing more food could start with something as simple as keeping more rainwater in the ground. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Britain brought back wild bison after 6,000 years; their grazing could create new habitats
item.description: The historic return of wild bison to Britain, absent for 6,000 years, is made possible by the Blean Bison Project. This initiative not only aims to reinstate these creatures but also to rejuvenate the woodland ecosystem they inhabit. Through their natural grazing and movements, they are instrumental in creating diverse habitats that support biodiversity. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: When bad luck isn't random: Understanding 'zemblanity'
item.description: In 2025, associate professor Christian Busch's Palisades home burned down in one of the most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history. Busch says the disaster wasn't blind bad luck; it was a clear case of "zemblanity," which he defines as a patterned and preventable form of misfortune built into the way a system, organization or individual operates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Directo Latam y la situación en Pereira un mes después del terremoto de 7,4 en Colombia
item.description: Un mes después del terremoto de 7,4 que sacudió a Colombia, miles de damnificados ahora enfrentan una grave crisis de vivienda, que los tiene viviendo temporalmente en refugios improvisados y en los hogares de familiares y amigos. Desde Pereira, una de las ciudades más golpeadas por el sismo, nuestro enviado especial Maxime Pluvinet nos contó cuál es la situación actual de las víctimas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: People in the US: how have you coped during this summer of record heat?
item.description: We’d like to hear from people about the impact of extreme heat this summer – and if you’ve had your power cut It’s been a record summer of heat in the US with rolling heat domes and July being the hottest month ever recorded in the country , surpassing temperatures stretching back over 132 years of reliable measurements, to 1895. July’s temperatures surpassed previous high marks set in July 1936, in the teeth of dust bowl conditions, and in July 2012. We want to hear from people across the US on how they have coped with the heat – and what it has meant for utility bills. Has the heat affected… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: English winemakers expect ‘vintage year’ after record-breaking summer heat
item.description: Hot weather means sweeter grapes, but outlook gloomier for beermakers, as drought diminishes barley harvest English sparkling winemakers expect their earliest grape harvest and a “vintage year” after a scorching summer quickly ripened grapes. However, beer sellers have warned of a potential shortage after record-breaking temperatures and a drought hitting much of England has caused poor yields of barley. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Hawaii has often dodged the path of hurricanes. Why did it see so many storms this summer?
item.description: Despite its location, the island chain has avoided the worst effects, but Hurricanes Lowell and Lala left a trail of damage this year Hurricane Lowell surged near the Hawaiian Islands this week, leaving a trail of downed trees and power lines, crumbled roads, sunken boats and destroyed piers on the island of Kauai. Residents were left to grapple not only with the damage, but the rising risks to the tropical archipelago as sea surface temperatures climb. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
